newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-NO PLACE TO HIDE, WARNS IRISH COACH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NO PLACE TO HIDE, WARNS IRISH COACH.

text.p: Ireland coach Brian Ashton has urged his players to frighten the life out of France when they launch their Five Nations campaign at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.
"As long as I can remember when England players went to play in Dublin, they knew they would get a match and what to expect. The Irish were a frightening sight," Ashton said.
"I do not like players to hide. I like players who stay up front and take personal responsibility. I like a game that is exciting for the players to play and is equally exciting to watch," he added.
Ashton, 50, quit as coach of English club champions Bath less than a fortnight ago and was appointed Ireland coach inside four days following the resignation of New Zealander Murray Kidd.
Under Kidd, who was appointed as the country's first full-time coach 15 months ago, Ireland lost six of their last seven internationals, including a 37-29 defeat by Italy on January 4.
Fly-half Eric Elwood, who last played for Ireland against Scotland a year ago, has been recalled to a side which shows five changes, one positional, in the team to meet France.
Maurice Field replaces the injured Mark McCall at centre and Niall Hogan regains his place at scrum-half in place of Stephen McIvor.
Paddy Johns takes over from Gabriel Fulcher in the second row while Denis McBride comes in at open-side flanker in the place of Eric Miller who moves to number eight at the expense of Anthony Foley.
Ashton declined to reveal any of his plans for the French match. "I do not like the phrase game-plan, but you adopt different methods and tactics related to the opposition."
Ireland's last win over the French in the Five Nations was at Lansdowne Road in 1983 and their best result since then was a draw in 1985.
For the first time since the 1995 World Cup, France welcome back scrum-half Fabien Galthie who has yet to play three tests in a row since his debut in 1991.
"I'm getting philosophical about it all," said the 27-year-old Galthie. "It comes and goes. Now I feel I've matured and I'm able to give my best, but you will judge."

Coach Jean-Claude Skrela said he was not expecting an easy match. "We must not underrate them. It would be a gross mistake to take them lightly. It's a team with qualities and especially a lot of spirit."
The match will mark the debut of assistant coach Pierre Villepreux, the man whose methods made Toulouse the best French club in the last decade.
"I'm sure he can bring us a lot," said Toulouse centre Thomas Castaignede. "He's respected by the players and when he talks, we listen."
